topic: Ambedkar & the Making of the Constitution

items.question: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
items.explanation:
**Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** chaired the seven-member Drafting Committee and is popularly called the 'Father of the Indian Constitution'.

**Why not the others**
- Dr. Rajendra Prasad — permanent President of the Constituent Assembly, not the drafting chairman.
- Jawaharlal Nehru — moved the Objectives Resolution and chaired the Union Powers and Union Constitution committees.
- Sir B.N. Rau — the Constitutional Advisor who prepared the initial draft, but was an adviser, not a member of the Assembly.

**Key facts**
- The Drafting Committee was set up on 29 August 1947.
- Ambedkar was also independent India's first Law Minister.

*Source: local APPSC GK PDF — Indian Polity: Making of the Constitution (Drafting Committee).*

covers: Drafting Committee — Ambedkar as chairman & its seven members (29 Aug 1947)

items.question: On which date did the Constitution of India come into force?
items.explanation:
The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 but **came into force on 26 January 1950**, chosen to honour the 1930 Purna Swaraj (Independence Day) declaration.

**Why not the others**
- 26 November 1949 — the date the Assembly adopted/enacted the Constitution (now Constitution Day).
- 15 August 1947 — India's independence (transfer of power), not the Constitution's commencement.
- 22 January 1947 — the day the Objectives Resolution was passed.

**Key facts**
- Adopted 26 Nov 1949 → enforced 26 Jan 1950.
- The gap allowed final signing and preparation.

*Source: local APPSC GK PDF — Indian Polity: Making of the Constitution (Timeline).*

items.question: The Poona Pact of 1932 was signed between Mahatma Gandhi and:
items.explanation:
The **Poona Pact (Sept 1932)** was concluded with **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**, who accepted reserved seats for the Depressed Classes within a joint electorate in place of separate electorates.

**Why not the others**
- Muhammad Ali Jinnah — led the Muslim League; associated with the Lucknow Pact (1916) and Two-Nation demand.
- Jawaharlal Nehru — not a signatory to the Poona Pact.
- Madan Mohan Malaviya — signed on behalf of the caste-Hindus, but the pact was fundamentally the Gandhi–Ambedkar agreement.

**Key facts**
- Triggered by Gandhi's fast-unto-death in Yerwada Jail against the Communal Award's separate electorates.
- Reserved seats for Depressed Classes in provincial legislatures rose from 71 to 148.

*Source: standard modern-history record (Poona Pact, 1932).*

covers: Poona Pact (1932) with Gandhi — reserved seats replace separate electorates

items.question:
Consider the following statements about the early life and education of B.R. Ambedkar:
1. He was born in 1891 at Mhow in a Mahar family.
2. He earned a doctorate in economics from Columbia University, New York.
3. He was called to the Bar from Gray's Inn, London.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
items.explanation:
All three are correct: Ambedkar was born on 14 April 1891 at **Mhow** (Madhya Pradesh) in the **Mahar** caste, took a **PhD in economics from Columbia**, and qualified as a **barrister at Gray's Inn**.

**Why not the others**
- 1 and 2 only — omits the Gray's Inn bar qualification, which is correct.
- 2 and 3 only — omits his birth details, which are correct.
- 1 and 3 only — omits the Columbia doctorate, which is correct.

**Key facts**
| Milestone | Detail |
|---|---|
| Born | 14 Apr 1891, Mhow |
| US study | MA & PhD, Columbia University |
| UK study | D.Sc., London School of Economics; Barrister, Gray's Inn |

*Source: standard biographical record (B.R. Ambedkar).*
items.source: standard biographical record — B.R. Ambedkar
covers: Ambedkar early life & education (1891 Mhow; Columbia, LSE, Gray's Inn)

items.question: The Mahad Satyagraha (1927) led by Ambedkar was launched primarily to:
options: Secure temple entry for Dalits at Nashik
Assert the right of the Depressed Classes to draw water from a public tank
Demand separate electorates at the Round Table Conference
items.explanation:
The **Mahad Satyagraha** asserted the right of the Depressed Classes to use water from the public **Chavdar tank** at Mahad — a landmark assertion of civic equality.

**Why not the others**
- Temple entry at Nashik — that was the later Kalaram Temple Entry movement (1930).
- Separate electorates at the Round Table — a constitutional demand (1930–32), not the Mahad water-rights protest.
- Oppose the Hindu Code Bill — Ambedkar championed the Bill; his 1951 resignation followed its stalling.

**Key facts**
- Chavdar tank agitation began 20 March 1927.
- At a second Mahad conference (25 Dec 1927), the Manusmriti was publicly burned as a symbol of caste oppression.

*Source: standard modern-history record (Mahad Satyagraha, 1927).*
items.source: standard modern-history record — Mahad Satyagraha 1927
covers: Mahad Satyagraha (1927) — Chavdar tank & Manusmriti burning

items.question: The Kalaram Temple Entry Satyagraha (1930) associated with Ambedkar took place at:
items.explanation:
The **Kalaram Temple Entry movement** began in 1930 at the Kalaram temple in **Nashik**, demanding entry for the Depressed Classes into the shrine.

**Why not the others**
- Mahad — the site of the 1927 water-rights (Chavdar tank) satyagraha, not the temple-entry stir.
- Vaikom — the Vaikom Satyagraha (1924–25) in Travancore was led by Kerala reformers (Periyar, K.P. Kesava Menon).
- Amravati — the Ambadevi temple agitation occurred there but the celebrated Ambedkar-led temple movement is the Nashik Kalaram one.

**Key facts**
- Kalaram Satyagraha launched 2 March 1930.
- Part of Ambedkar's broader campaign for social/religious equality alongside civic rights.

*Source: standard modern-history record (Kalaram Temple Entry, 1930).*
items.source: standard modern-history record — Kalaram Temple Entry 1930
covers: Kalaram Temple Entry movement (Nashik 1930)

items.question:
Match List-I (Ambedkar's initiative) with List-II (Detail):
List-I
A. Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha
B. Mooknayak
C. Bahishkrit Bharat
D. Prabuddha Bharat
List-II
1. First journal (1920), aided by Shahu of Kolhapur
2. Social-welfare organisation (1924)
3. Marathi fortnightly (1927)
4. Later journal reflecting Buddhist turn (1956)
items.explanation:
Ambedkar founded the **Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha (1924)** to uplift the Depressed Classes, and used journals to mobilise opinion: **Mooknayak (1920)**, **Bahishkrit Bharat (1927)** and later **Prabuddha Bharat (1956)**.

**Why not the others**
- A-1, B-2, C-4, D-3 — swaps the Sabha with Mooknayak and misdates the journals.
- A-2, B-3, C-1, D-4 — reverses Mooknayak (1920) and Bahishkrit Bharat (1927).
- A-3, B-1, C-2, D-4 — wrongly labels the Sabha as a 1927 fortnightly.

**Key facts**
| Item | Year |
|---|---|
| Mooknayak | 1920 |
| Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha | 1924 |
| Bahishkrit Bharat | 1927 |
| Janata / Prabuddha Bharat | 1930 / 1956 |

*Source: standard modern-history record (Ambedkar's organisations & press).*
items.source: standard modern-history record — Ambedkar's organisations & press
covers: Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha & journals (Mooknayak, Bahishkrit Bharat)

items.question: The Communal Award of 1932, which Ambedkar had sought at the Round Table Conferences, provided the Depressed Classes with:
options: Reserved seats within a joint electorate
Nominated seats in the Viceroy's council
A quota in government services only
items.explanation:
Ramsay MacDonald's **Communal Award (Aug 1932)** granted the Depressed Classes **separate electorates**, meeting Ambedkar's demand pressed at the Round Table Conferences.

**Why not the others**
- Reserved seats within a joint electorate — this was the outcome of the Poona Pact, which replaced the Award's separate electorates.
- Nominated seats in the Viceroy's council — not what the Award provided for Depressed Classes.
- A quota in services only — the Award concerned electoral representation, not merely jobs.

**Key facts**
- Ambedkar attended all three Round Table Conferences (1930–32) as a Depressed Classes representative.
- Gandhi opposed separate electorates for Depressed Classes, precipitating the Poona Pact.

*Source: standard modern-history record (Communal Award, 1932).*
items.source: standard modern-history record — Communal Award 1932
covers: Round Table Conferences & separate-electorate demand; Communal Award (1932)

items.question:
Match List-I (Political party/organisation) with List-II (Year founded by Ambedkar):
List-I
A. Independent Labour Party
B. Scheduled Castes Federation
C. Republican Party of India
List-II
1. 1936
2. 1942
3. 1956 (realised 1957)
items.explanation:
Ambedkar's political vehicles evolved over time: the **Independent Labour Party (1936)**, the **Scheduled Castes Federation (1942)**, and finally the **Republican Party of India**, conceived in 1956 and formed in 1957 after his death.

**Why not the others**
- A-2, B-1, C-3 — reverses ILP (1936) and SCF (1942).
- A-3, B-2, C-1 — misdates the ILP to 1956 and RPI to 1936.
- A-1, B-3, C-2 — misplaces SCF and RPI years.

**Key facts**
- ILP contested the 1937 Bombay provincial elections successfully.
- The RPI's founding was announced in his final writings; it was launched posthumously.

*Source: standard modern-history record (Ambedkar's political parties).*
items.source: standard modern-history record — Ambedkar's political parties
covers: Ambedkar's parties (Independent Labour Party, Scheduled Castes Federation, RPI)

items.question: The work 'Annihilation of Caste' (1936) by Ambedkar was originally:
options: His presidential address to the Indian National Congress
An undelivered speech prepared for the Jat-Pat-Todak Mandal, Lahore
A memorandum submitted to the Simon Commission
A judgment written as Law Minister
items.explanation:
**Annihilation of Caste** was an **undelivered address** written for the **Jat-Pat-Todak Mandal** of Lahore in 1936; the organisers withdrew the invitation over its radical content, and Ambedkar published it himself.

**Why not the others**
- INC presidential address — Ambedkar was never Congress president; he was often at odds with it.
- Memorandum to the Simon Commission — he did testify before it, but that is separate from this text.
- A judgment as Law Minister — the work predates independence and is a social-reform tract, not a judgment.

**Key facts**
- His economics writings include The Problem of the Rupee (his London thesis) and The Evolution of Provincial Finance in British India.
- Later works include Who Were the Shudras? and The Buddha and His Dhamma.

*Source: standard record (Ambedkar's writings).*
items.source: standard record — Ambedkar's writings
covers: Ambedkar's writings — Annihilation of Caste, The Problem of the Rupee

items.question:
Consider the following statements about the origin of the Constituent Assembly:
1. The idea of a Constituent Assembly was first put forward by M.N. Roy in 1934.
2. The Assembly was finally constituted under the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946.
3. Elections to the Assembly were held on the basis of universal adult franchise.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
items.explanation:
Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Constituent Assembly idea came from **M.N. Roy (1934)** and it was set up under the **Cabinet Mission Plan (1946)**. Statement 3 is wrong — members were **indirectly elected by provincial legislative assemblies**, not by universal adult franchise.

**Why not the others**
- 1 and 3 only — statement 3 is false, so this fails.
- 2 and 3 only — again includes the false statement 3.
- 1, 2 and 3 — statement 3 is incorrect.

**Key facts**
- INC formally demanded a Constituent Assembly in 1935; Nehru insisted on elected members in 1938.
- Elections were held in July 1946; the first meeting was on 9 December 1946.

*Source: local APPSC GK PDF — Indian Polity: Making of the Constitution (Demand for Constituent Assembly).*
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Indian Polity: Making of the Constitution (Demand for Constituent Assembly)
covers: Demand & evolution of the Constituent Assembly (M.N. Roy 1934 → Cabinet Mission 1946)

items.question:
Consider the following statements about the composition of the Constituent Assembly:
1. Its total strength as originally planned was 389 seats.
2. Of these, 93 seats were allotted to the princely states.
3. After the partition of India its effective strength was reduced to 299.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
items.explanation:
All three are correct. The Assembly was designed with **389 seats** (292 British provinces + 4 chief commissioners' provinces + **93 princely states**); after **partition** the number fell to **299**.

**Why not the others**
- 1 and 3 only — leaves out the correct 93-seat princely-states figure.
- 2 and 3 only — leaves out the correct 389 total.
- 1 and 2 only — leaves out the correct post-partition figure of 299.

**Key facts**
| Category | Seats |
|---|---|
| British provinces | 292 |
| Chief commissioners' provinces | 4 |
| Princely states | 93 |
| Total → after partition | 389 → 299 |

Seats were filled by proportional representation with a single transferable vote (1 seat ≈ 10 lakh people).

*Source: local APPSC GK PDF — Indian Polity: Making of the Constitution (Composition).*
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Indian Polity: Making of the Constitution (Composition)
covers: Composition of the Constituent Assembly (389 → 299 seats; election method)

items.question:
Match List-I (Office in the Constituent Assembly) with List-II (Person):
List-I
A. First (provisional) President
B. Permanent President
C. Vice-President
D. Constitutional Advisor
List-II
1. Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha
2. Dr. Rajendra Prasad
3. H.C. Mukherjee
4. Sir B.N. Rau
items.explanation:
The Assembly's first (provisional) President was **Sachchidananda Sinha** (9 Dec 1946); **Rajendra Prasad** became permanent President (11 Dec 1946), with **H.C. Mukherjee** as Vice-President and **B.N. Rau** as Constitutional Advisor.

**Why not the others**
- A-2, B-1, C-3, D-4 — reverses Sinha and Rajendra Prasad.
- A-1, B-2, C-4, D-3 — swaps Mukherjee and B.N. Rau.
- A-3, B-2, C-1, D-4 — wrongly makes Mukherjee the provisional President.

**Key facts**
- Sinha presided as the oldest member (a convention borrowed from other assemblies).
- Rajendra Prasad later became independent India's first President.

*Source: local APPSC GK PDF — Indian Polity: Making of the Constitution (Office-bearers).*
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Indian Polity: Making of the Constitution (Office-bearers)
covers: First meeting & office-bearers (Sinha, Rajendra Prasad, Mukherjee, B.N. Rau)

items.question: The Objectives Resolution, which laid down the philosophical foundations of the Constitution, was moved in the Constituent Assembly by:
items.explanation:
**Jawaharlal Nehru** moved the **Objectives Resolution on 13 December 1946**; it was adopted on 22 January 1947 and became the basis of the Preamble.

**Why not the others**
- Ambedkar on 29 Aug 1947 — that date is when the Drafting Committee was constituted, not the Objectives Resolution.
- Patel on 22 Jan 1947 — 22 Jan 1947 is the date the Resolution was passed, but Patel did not move it.
- Rajendra Prasad on 26 Nov 1949 — that is the date the Constitution was adopted.

**Key facts**
- The Resolution declared India an independent sovereign republic.
- Its ideals were carried into the Preamble largely intact.

*Source: local APPSC GK PDF — Indian Polity: Making of the Constitution (Objectives Resolution).*
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Indian Polity: Making of the Constitution (Objectives Resolution)
covers: Objective Resolution (Nehru, 13 Dec 1946; passed 22 Jan 1947)

items.question: Who among the following was NOT a member of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution?
items.explanation:
**Sardar Patel** was NOT on the Drafting Committee; he chaired the Advisory, States and Provincial committees. The seven-member Drafting Committee comprised Ambedkar (chair), K.M. Munshi, Alladi Krishnaswamy Ayyar, N. Gopalaswamy Ayyangar, Syed Mohammad Saadulla, N. Madhava Rau and T.T. Krishnamachari.

**Why not the others**
- Alladi Krishnaswamy Ayyar — eminent jurist of the Madras Presidency; a drafting member.
- N. Gopalaswamy Ayyangar — drafting member; later a Union minister.
- K.M. Munshi — drafting member; founder of Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan.

**Key facts**
- Drafting Committee set up 29 August 1947 with seven members.
- B.L. Mitter and D.P. Khaitan were replaced by N. Madhava Rau and T.T. Krishnamachari during its work.

*Source: local APPSC GK PDF — Indian Polity: Making of the Constitution (Drafting Committee members).*
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Indian Polity: Making of the Constitution (Drafting Committee members)
covers: Drafting Committee — Ambedkar as chairman & its seven members (29 Aug 1947)

items.question:
Match List-I (Committee of the Constituent Assembly) with List-II (Chairman):
List-I
A. Union Powers Committee
B. Drafting Committee
C. States Committee (for negotiating with states)
D. Rules of Procedure Committee
List-II
1. Jawaharlal Nehru
2. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
3. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
4. Dr. Rajendra Prasad
items.explanation:
**Nehru** chaired the Union Powers (and Union Constitution) committees, **Ambedkar** the Drafting Committee, **Patel** the States, Provincial and Advisory committees, and **Rajendra Prasad** the Rules of Procedure committee.

**Why not the others**
- A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3 — swaps Nehru and Ambedkar and misassigns the rest.
- A-1, B-2, C-4, D-3 — wrongly gives the States Committee to Rajendra Prasad.
- A-3, B-2, C-1, D-4 — wrongly makes Patel chair the Union Powers Committee.

**Key facts**
- The Assembly had 8 major and several minor committees.
- Patel's leadership of the States/Advisory committees underpinned the integration of princely states.

*Source: local APPSC GK PDF — Indian Polity: Making of the Constitution (Important Committees).*
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Indian Polity: Making of the Constitution (Important Committees)
covers: Major committees of the Assembly & their chairmen

items.question: Which of the following members of the Constituent Assembly hailed from the Andhra/Telugu region and founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha?
items.explanation:
**Durgabai Deshmukh**, a lawyer and women's-rights activist from the Andhra region, founded the **Andhra Mahila Sabha** and later chaired the Central Social Welfare Board.

**Why not the others**
- Sarojini Naidu — poet-leader from Hyderabad who became Governor of UP, but not the Andhra Mahila Sabha's founder.
- Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit — Nehru's sister and diplomat, not associated with the Andhra Mahila Sabha.
- Hansa Mehta — Assembly member from Bombay known for gender-equal wording of rights, not from Andhra.

**Key facts — other Andhra members**
| Member | Note |
|---|---|
| Alladi Krishnaswamy Ayyar | Jurist; Drafting Committee |
| N.G. Ranga | Peasant leader |
| Pattabhi Sitaramayya | Congress historian |
| T. Prakasam | 'Andhra Kesari'; first CM of Andhra State |

*Source: local APPSC GK PDF — Indian Polity: Making of the Constitution (Important members) + standard record.*

items.question:
Consider the following statements about Ambedkar's role after independence:
1. He was the first Law Minister of independent India.
2. He resigned from the Union Cabinet in 1951, partly over the stalling of the Hindu Code Bill.
3. In 1956 he embraced Buddhism at Nagpur.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
items.explanation:
All three are correct: Ambedkar was independent India's **first Law Minister**, **resigned in 1951** (his grievances included the shelving of the **Hindu Code Bill**), and **converted to Buddhism at Nagpur in October 1956**.

**Why not the others**
- 1 and 2 only — omits the 1956 Buddhist conversion, which is correct.
- 2 and 3 only — omits his first-Law-Minister role, which is correct.
- 1 and 3 only — omits the 1951 resignation, which is correct.

**Key facts**
- Converted with lakhs of followers at Deekshabhoomi, Nagpur, on 14 Oct 1956.
- Died on 6 December 1956 (Mahaparinirvan Diwas); awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 1990.

*Source: standard record (Ambedkar's later career).*
items.source: standard record — Ambedkar's later career
covers: Ambedkar as first Law Minister; Hindu Code Bill resignation & 1956 Buddhist conversion

items.question: With reference to the making of the Constitution, which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
options: K.C. Neogy — Member of the Constituent Assembly
Sachchidananda Sinha — Permanent President of the Constituent Assembly
B.N. Rau — Chairman of the Drafting Committee
items.explanation:
**K.C. Neogy was a member of the Constituent Assembly** (and later chaired the First Finance Commission, 1951), so this pair is correct.

**Why not the others**
- Sachchidananda Sinha — was only the *provisional/first* President; the *permanent* President was Dr. Rajendra Prasad.
- B.N. Rau — was the *Constitutional Advisor*, not the Drafting Committee chairman (that was Ambedkar).
- H.C. Mukherjee — was the *Vice-President* of the Assembly, not the Constitutional Advisor.

**Key facts**
- The National Flag was adopted on 22 July 1947; the National Anthem and Song on 24 January 1950.
- The Assembly acted as the provisional Parliament until the 1951–52 elections.

*Source: Standard references — Constituent Assembly membership; UPSC 2019 PYQ.*
items.source: Standard references — Constituent Assembly membership
covers: Other CA members (K.C. Neogy → First Finance Commission; H.C. Mukherjee; Frank Anthony) & national symbols (flag 22 Jul 1947, anthem/song 24 Jan 1950)

items.question: The Constituent Assembly adopted the National Flag of India on:
items.explanation:
The Constituent Assembly adopted the **National Flag on 22 July 1947**, before independence.

**Why not the others**
- 26 November 1949 — the date the Constitution was adopted/enacted.
- 15 August 1947 — Independence Day, but the flag had already been adopted on 22 July.
- 24 January 1950 — when the National Anthem and National Song were adopted (and members signed the Constitution).

**Key facts**
- The Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950.
- The State Emblem (Lion Capital of Sarnath) was adopted on 26 January 1950.

*Source: Standard references — national symbols adopted by the Constituent Assembly.*
